conviction_note: Caleres reported yesterday morning with Famous Footwear -5.9% comp in exactly SHOE's fiscal quarter (both ended 2026-08-01) versus -2.3% in Q1 when SHOE printed -2.1%; consensus revenue of $299.19m embeds only -2.4% YoY, so the top line is set up to miss by 3-4% — sized down from -5 to -3.5 because the reconstructed SCVL base rate is only ~6% absolute, the stock is already at a 52-week low, and the same later-back-to-school mechanism hands management a genuinely good August to talk about on a guide that is explicitly back-half loaded.

findings.finding: Caleres reported 2026-09-09 that Famous Footwear comparable sales fell 5.9% in the quarter ended 2026-08-01 — the identical fiscal window to SHOE's Q2 — blaming 'a later Back-to-School season and softness in lifestyle athletic'; Famous Footwear comped -2.3% in Q1 against Shoe Carnival's -2.1%, so the two banners were running in lockstep before this 360bp step-down, while SHOE's Q2 revenue consensus of $299.19m implies only about -2.4% YoY.
findings.why_not_priced: Caleres' headline was an EPS beat and a raised floor, and CAL traded up on it; SHOE closed -0.67% on the day the datapoint landed and is still up 4.1% over five sessions. If the market had read the Famous Footwear line as a comp read-through, SHOE would have broken its 52-week low of $12.78 on 09-09 rather than sitting a fraction above it, and the sell-side note flow would show Q2 revenue cuts after 09-09 rather than the last visible action being a Williams Trading target cut dated ~09-02 that still carries a Buy. Both causes Caleres named are channel-wide, not company-specific, and SHOE is more exposed to them than Famous Footwear: management said on the Q1 call that back-to-school 'begins the third week of July, and it really is an August play' and that '70% of our business is still athletic during that time period' — a later back-to-school and soft lifestyle athletic hit precisely SHOE's Q2 mix.
findings.independence: Genesco, quarter also ended 2026-08-01, reported 2026-09-03 that consolidated comps fell 1% and that it CUT its full-year comp guidance to flat from +1-2%, corroborating that the May-July window itself was weak in footwear retail: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018498/000119312526381023/gco-ex99_1.htm . Management's own 70%-athletic and August-play quotes are from a third document, the 2026-05-21 Q1 call transcript: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/21/shoe-carnival-scvl-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/

findings.finding: SHOE has no IEEPA tariff-refund windfall available to cushion the quarter — its 10-K states 'Substantially all of our footwear product is manufactured overseas, including the merchandise we purchase from domestic vendors and the smaller portion we import directly from overseas manufacturers', so it is importer of record on only a small slice, whereas Caleres booked $55.6m of IEEPA recoveries plus $1.8m interest in the very quarter whose beat is being read across to SHOE.
findings.why_not_priced: SHOE's Q1 10-Q filed 2026-06-05 carries no tariff receivable and the 2026-05-21 call spoke of tariffs only as ongoing 'average unit cost pressures' — three months after the Supreme Court struck IEEPA on 2026-02-20 and a month after CBP opened the CAPE refund process. If the market expected a refund, the stock would not be making 52-week lows into a print with $116m of cash and a debt-free balance sheet, and the FY gross margin guide of ~34% (-260bp) would have been challenged as stale rather than reaffirmed unremarked. The asymmetry is the point: the part of Caleres' print SHOE shares is the retail banner that comped -5.9%, and the parts that produced the beat — the refund and a +23.6% brand portfolio — SHOE does not have, which also removes the mechanism Caleres used to lift its full-year floor.
findings.independence: SOURCE CLUSTER NOTE: the $55.6m refund figure comes from the same Caleres 8-K as finding 1 and should be collapsed with it; the load-bearing, independent element here is the 10-K sourcing language and the absence of any tariff receivable in the Q1 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000895447/000119312526258362/scvl-20260502.htm (filed 2026-06-05).

findings.finding: The same later-back-to-school shift that damages SHOE's Q2 lands squarely in its Q3: Genesco said on 2026-09-03 that Journeys accelerated to a mid-single-digit comp in August and raised its FY EPS outlook to the high end, and Caleres said Famous Footwear comps are flat quarter-to-date through Labor Day — a 590bp sequential improvement — so SHOE, whose FY2026 guide of $1.40-$1.60 was explicitly framed as 'down first half and then up second half', has a credible constructive August update to give from a 52-week low.
findings.why_not_priced: SHOE fell from $16.11 on 08-10 to $12.84 on 09-01, -20% on no company news at all — no 8-K since 06-11 and no Form 4 since 06-22 — which is the market pricing a bad quarter without pricing the offsetting Q3 handoff. If the August handoff were priced, SHOE would not be trading within 4% of its 52-week low three sessions after the two most comparable retailers both described August as materially better than May-July. This is the mechanism by which a revenue miss can still produce an up day, exactly as it did for CAL on 09-09.
findings.independence: Caleres' 'quarter to date through Labor Day, Famous Footwear comparable store sales are flat' is in a different filing, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000014707/000001470726000138/cal-20260909xex99d1.htm (2026-09-09) — note this is the same document as finding 1 and points the opposite way, which is why finding 1 is sized below the raw comp read-through.

findings.finding: The baseline's put/call open-interest ratio of 26.6 on 28,591 contracts is a data artifact, not a positioning signal: the actual 2026-09-18 chain carries open interest in the hundreds, roughly 488 puts against 309 calls across the strikes shown, a ratio near 1.6.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a correction to the baseline rather than a market inefficiency, and it should be recorded so no downstream reader treats it as evidence. 28,591 contracts would be 2.86m shares of exposure, about 3.6 days of the 788,765-share ADV and roughly 10% of shares outstanding, in a name whose ATM bid-ask is 91% of mid and whose ATM IV prints at 184.9% — the same vendor feed producing all three numbers is unusable, most likely stitched across the 2026-06-12 SCVL-to-SHOE ticker change. Nothing in the price needs to change; what changes is that the loudest number in the baseline carries no information.

searched_and_found_nothing: Any 8-K, pre-announcement or guidance update since the 2026-06-11 name-change filing — EDGAR shows nothing on CIK 895447 after that except two routine 13G/A amendments on 2026-07-14
Insider buying at the 52-week low — no Form 4 on this CIK since 2026-06-22, despite the stock falling from $16.11 to $12.84 in August
An explanation for the -8.39% single session on 2026-08-25 and the -4.90% on 2026-09-08 — no company news, no filing and no dated analyst action found for either date
A permanent CEO announcement — Cliff Sifford has been interim since 2026-02-24 and the search is still open, so a named successor alongside the print is a live but unforecastable catalyst
Local-press evidence of store closures beyond the guided 12-14 for FY2026 that would imply a larger Q2 impairment charge
Any SHOE-specific IEEPA refund claim, receivable or CBP CAPE filing
A usable option-implied move — the front chain's spread is 91% of mid and Yahoo, Barchart and Nasdaq option pages were unreachable or empty
Designer Brands as a same-day read — DBI also reports 2026-09-10, so it offers no pre-print information
baseline_tension: The baseline's empty history is recoverable and it matters: under SCVL this company moved -6.0% on 2025-11-20, roughly -6.4% pre-market to -8.1% close on its 2026-03-26 Q4 print, +3.3% on 2026-05-21 and +5.9% on its 2025 Q1 print, so a ~6% absolute reaction is the base rate and the 3.29% deadband is about half of it — and critically, the two down prints came on revenue misses despite EPS beats, which is exactly the shape the Famous Footwear read implies; against that, my negative lean cuts directly against the run-up control the repo says has been the day's best free ranker (run_up_20d of -15.16% and a 52-week low argue for a bounce), and the skew is unmeasurable, so I have sized down to -3.5 rather than the -5 the comp read-through alone would justify.
